Solo bicycle touring can be an extreme form of adventure tourism. If you do it long enough, and hard enough, it will cause you to look deep inside yourself for answers to life's basic questions.

It can be dangerous as well as fun and rewarding, but you must be properly prepared and trained in the necessary skills.

We are planning a short course on how to do it successfully, with a short beginners tour to follow.
Anyone who wants to join in a tour with us must be prepared through our course training.  This 'Bicycle Journey' telegram group is necessary reading if you want to learn solo touring.

Sela and Panha Suon will be organizing the course and the rides, and I will be the instructor and consultant.

It can be dangerous, but only if you are not adequately prepared,  so join with us at your own risk!

Also, there will be expenses involved depending on how much equipment you need.

Many nice people, but every time I come to Thailand I feel I've had enough. Really, I've had enough of Asian culture.  Too loud, and too polluted.
I appreciate many qualities of Asian people, but quality of life is intolerable much of the time - it is the reason I never leave my office in pp except at 4 am to 6 am.
Asians have no concern for noise and air pollution, which are both inescapable, as well as detrimental to quality of life.  This is so unfortunate.

Learn to judge an urban area by studying maps.  All urban areas have similarities.
Compare CM to CR on the map.  Notice what we call 'ring roads' or beltways.  Some cities have 2 or 3 beltways. If no beltway, then typically a small city.  Some have partial beltways.

Absolutely unbelievable how stupid and senseless a society can be.  And these are the results we get when we give such people technology they neither deserve or understand.  The future will hold even greater nightmares.

I can only ask myself, what can I personally learn from this?  I believe there are subversive cultural wars underway, while the masses of ordinary people are mentally and intellectually brain dead.

Never again will I return to Thailand to be among the ordinary people. Anyone who is awake, alert and aware must be protected from the social environment they create for themselves.

A sane and truly compassionate people would never even think to inflict such behavior upon their friends and neighbors.

This is how the cultural war works - 

Destroy their traditional culture by overwhelming them with technology they neither need or understand, and do it in such a way so that they believe they are continuing to engage and promote their traditional culture, while at the same time making them work and pay for the technology they are using to destroy themselves.

What better way to win a war, destroy and weaken a nation than to cause the ordinary people to commit cultural suicide?

At first I felt these were isolated incidents, but it is plain to see now the behavior is widespread throughout SE Asia.  Then I thought maybe such behavior was an emerging cultural phenomenon, but now I am realizing this is all about war and cultural destruction to weaken a people into economic servitude.

99% of the amplification equipment in the marketplace and out in the public domain is unneeded and unnecessary, while at the same time it serves as nothing more than a public nuisance.

Explain to me the benefits and sanity in all of this. One o'clock in the morning, and just another ordinary Thai (SE Asia) village, like tens of thousands of others.  

And the noise just not originate from one location.  This sick behavior is widespread among all the community, and all the communities.
 
And not one person complains or does a thing to make a difference.  There is absolutely no social good to be found in the behavior of these ordinary, common people.
Those that are good, and there are many, have become completely stupified into submission.
And all at the same time, the lingering stench of burning trash and plastic.

People use amplification equipment for one reason - it makes them feel, powerful, important, and pervasive, when in actuality it makes them weak and ineffectual.

Surely this will continue until 2 am, and then of course some other idiot somewhere nearby in the soundscape will start it all up again at 5 am, if not 4 am.

What kind of sick society is this? How can anyone who ares about people and community allow this to continue?

For these reasons I will leave this part of the world and glad fully never again return. Whenever I end up, I will feel joy not to be here.
6 am and the noise never stopped throughout the night.

Irrespective of the noise pollution, animal control issues, and burning of trash, Thai people can be counted among the most kind and generous people of the world. At this time in history, there is great abundance in Thailand, and it is through this great abundance that both the good and bad in people shine through.

So I would not want to discourage anyone from traveling in Thailand, or exploring the Thai experience, for as long as you find it tolerable.

Of course, being alone on a bicycle and always sleeping in the out of doors is a big part of my experience, along with being a foreigner on a strange bicycle and frequenting Buddhist temples over most all other places but the forests and whatever is left of the wilderness.

Do you ever think of all the wild animals which are becoming extinct each year due to the nature of man?

Why do you think hundreds of whales in the ocean would just suddenly decide to up and beach themselves to suicide?

I was of the understanding that whales are to be counted among the most intelligent species on earth.

Sometimes alone at nigh in the Thai wilderness I feel such as one of these wild animals that are about to become extinct.

It is said that all the of noises created by man and his monstrous machines bouncing around in the oceans and bringing the whales to a state of confusion and hopelessness.

Consumism is about feeding the masses of people so man toys and artificial stimuli, that it causes them to be in a state of confusion and give up all hope as well, eventually.

Wars often take years to build up and occur, and then there is the aftermath.

More wars will come and wars will go.  Do you think the wars of the future will be any different?  What sort of weapons will they use?

Sound warfare and psychological weapons?  What is to stop any single individual from playing this game?

A war on terror is a far on fear, and a war on fear is unthinkable, unwinnable, stupid, and a big lie.

Where has the US Military to have been known to use weapons of sound and psyops (psychological operations)?

The overall distance I did yesterday was about 160km, 60km from twon to the base of the mountain,  49 km to the top and back down.

The first 30 and a bit more km of climbing was ok. A fitter rider can do it with 11-28T rear cassette and 34T chain ring in the front. I used 11-32T and 34T. The last 10km or so was hard with 11-28T for me. I wwnted to challenge myself even I have 11-32T, but I was using 11-28T for almost the whole climb except the last 2km. In short, I would say almost everyone can climb up with 11-32T.

I left town at 5am, stopped and ate breakfast,  and reached the base at around 8am. I started climbing at 8:30am then reached the top at about 1:30am. I think it took me about 4h and half to climb to the top.

It was pretty cold, 17 degree celsius up top at 1:30pm. 
5Km before you reach the top, there is a pllace where the two huge budhhist stupas are. It's ​nice and beautiful with many colorful flower. 

When you reach the top, there is nothing much but a Astronomy Observatory station to me looks really cool, then a natural park.

The descending can go extremely fast depending on your confidence. I got it up to 82km/h, my new record. Keep in mind that it would be really dangerous even for me who already has a little bit of experience and skill with bicycle handling. I would not recommend to go that fast if it is your first time dewcending down there or if your bike is not in good shape. 

4 minute into the decending I went of the main road but managed to get back without getting into a crash. It was a bit scary. I think the key to this is to be calm and believe in yourself. Descending is a skill. There are guys who could go even over 80 km down that mountain. Anyway, I think you want to know your limit and push it, but not to push it too hard.
The time record of Doi Inthanon climbing is 1h59min, holded by Peter Pouly.

Overall, I think it was a memorable, fun, and challenging experience. Plus, it was really exausting. I think I did ok with the climb, but the descend was a bit far out of my comfort zone. Thus, I was not mentally prepared and not that relaxed. Anyway, I DID IT. Good news, it didn't cost me any money to get in. I feel we all can well appreciate the pristine beauty and tranquility of nature, and we all hate to see it destroyed.
But in fact it is being destroyed, everyday, and it will continue to be destroyed, unless people speak up and educate their neighbors about what is really going on in the world.
I would say there are few people in the world that know or have had a more intimate experience with roadside Cambodia than myself, and I include the vast majority of Cambodians.

Cambodia was recently completely destroyed, and only now is experiencing a rebirth.  This generation of Cambodian youth leaders I am working with are a very special generation, and more than any other generation to come, the future is up to this generation.

There is a concept I am teaching now, and it is called 'wild camping', 'free camping', or 'stealth camping'.  I am teaching this concept to a select group of students who want to know.  This type of camping is best done alone, which means it can be dangerous and a person needs plenty of courage and expertise.

Tom and Panha had advanced lessons with me in my office before we left on the trip.  One of the principles involved here is to be fully awake, alert and aware of all sounds happening around you, even as you sleep, as much as that is possible.

I think you may appreciate now why one does not really want to be tuning out noises as we are stealth camping.  Ideally, we should only be dealing with the sounds of nature, but add along with this the disruptive nature of omni-directional low-frequency infrasound, and a person can hardly get a good night's rest.

Barking dogs while you are trying to sleep are one thing, but dogs that run out into the street and chase you while snarling and growling are another.

I do not want to go deeply into why dogs behave as they do, but you know from Psych 101 (Pavlov) that they can be easily controlled by their owners if their owners had a half an ounce of common sense.

I asked him if he has some tips for me to improve myself toward achieving my dream. He suggests that I should train and starting involved in events or races to gauge my strenths and weaknesses. If I could get into international races, it is the best for me.
I can't really see the outside world and improve myself if I am just competing at national or local level. I have to go out. That is one of the problems Thai pro road racers are having now.

This is something interesting I have learned from him. He told me most of the professional bicycle teams in Thailand are somehow owned by military or the government. They almost have full control over those Thai cyclists. The strange thing is that the government seems to lack of commitment to get those Thai cyclists into international or world class level cycling.

He even told me that they don't want to send those Thai riders to compete in races outside of the country. In addition, the Thai riders seem to be satified and happy with what they are having at the moment. A lot of them end up becoming a police officers at the end. Then they get free insurance from the government, free public service, and some sort of support for their whole family.

In short, he siad their goals of joining or becoming a professional cyclists in Thailand is not to become a world pro cyclist but to actually get a position in the gov at the end. They don't have the dream like mine. I heard this clearly from him. He siad, "It took me a lot of time to understand this. They just don't like and are afraid to take risks. They want to do comfortable for them. I was trying to teach some Thai kids and bring them up to international stage, but that is not what they see or want."
From this, I would say he already gave up on trying to make a professional world class cyclist out of Thailand. He even said this is a fact for many countries in Asia except Japan.

I think this is a really big advantages I have over those Thai riders. I have the dreams and the heart. They don't.  In term of fitness, skill, and training, I think they are just more experienced and previlige than me.

I told Peter this. I said, "To be honest with you, I am really jealous with those Thai pro cyclists. They have the opportunity at hand, but they decide to choose the police officer path. It is realy sad."
I also learned something else about the difference in alttitude.

He siad it is not neccessary for me now to train in a high altitude. That is only if most of my races are taking place in high altitude places. The difference that the altitude traning makes is the quick addaptation. If a rider is living in a higher altitude, he seems to be able to adapt to the change in altitude of the race quicker and better, but that doesn't mean they are stronger on the flat.
Some riders have problem with the change in altitude when they go above 1000m or so.
He said I might want to vary my training between flat training and climbing, because I don't to go easy on the flat all the time.
I asked him do I have to move and train in Thailand. He said it is not neccessary, but I might want to join races in Thailand.
And the best is to join international and outside of the country races. I think he meant I need to compete with those from Europe or from countries where cycling is big.

I asked if there a possibility for Thai cyclist or Asian cyclists to become a world pros. He siad yes, but they have to forget about the government, the police officer position, the benifitw they get from serving the gov and their country and of course they become more couragous to take some risks.

They can just move out off Thailand to Europe. I could not find out why yet, but he said it is one of the means. The key is their decision whether or not they want to take professional cyclist path or police officer path.
I asked him also if there has been any professional world class team who shows interest in Thai riders. He said no.
Becuace, they are not experienced enough plus they don't get to expose themselves that much in outside races.

Wild-camping is allowed in Finland under a law. known as Everyman’s Law. This means that you are free to camp anywhere, as long as you are over 150 metres from any dwelling hous; even on private land! (There were periods during my journey where I met maybe 3 houses in 35 miles!

The terrain is dead flat. Every road has a cycle path off the road and running parallel to it. The weather is great in June. The people are really, really friendly and helpful to foreigners and I was offered many meals and accommodation for the night. I would say that 95% of them speak excellent English.

You need to secure both your front and rear wheels, or some thief will steal your wheel or wheels.

One good wheel and hub can cost 500 usd.

For best security, never let bike out of your sight, but that is not always possible.

Second best would be a cable lock that will wrap both wheels.
